cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R, R-module M and submodule U, the kernel of the canonical quotient map M → M/U is U.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the criterion for a class in a module quotient to be zero.
sketch_steps: Fix R, M and U without finiteness assumptions.
An element lies in the kernel exactly when its quotient class is zero.
The class is zero exactly when the element belongs to U.
Identify the two submodules by this membership equivalence.

cards.canonical_statement: Every canonical quotient map M → M/U of modules over a commutative ring is surjective.
cards.proof_strategy: Every quotient class has a representative in M.
sketch_steps: Fix a submodule U of M.
Take an arbitrary element of M/U.
Choose a representative x in M by quotient induction.
The canonical projection sends x to the chosen class.

cards.proof_strategy: The image of inclusion and the kernel of projection are both U.
sketch_steps: View U as an R-module with its induced structure.
The inclusion has image U in M.
The canonical quotient projection has kernel U.
Their equality proves exactness at M.

cards.canonical_statement: If an R-linear map f:M→N vanishes on a submodule U, there exists an R-linear map g:M/U→N whose composite with the quotient projection is f.
cards.proof_strategy: Descend f to quotient classes using U⊆ker(f) for representative independence.
sketch_steps: Assume U is contained in the kernel of f.
Define the image of a class [x] to be f(x).
Changing x by an element of U does not change f(x).
The descended map is linear and its composite with projection equals f.

cards.proof_strategy: Use surjectivity of the quotient projection to compare the maps on all classes.
sketch_steps: Take a class in M/U.
Choose a representative in M.
Apply the equality of composites to this representative.
Conclude the maps agree everywhere and use extensionality.

cards.canonical_statement: For submodules U,V of an R-module M, the inverse image of the image of V under M→M/U is U+V.
cards.proof_strategy: Elements with the same quotient class differ by an element of U.
sketch_steps: Project V to M/U and take its full inverse image.
Any element in that inverse image differs from an element of V by an element of U.
Thus it belongs to U+V.

cards.proof_strategy: Apply Nakayama's lemma in its Jacobson-radical form to the finitely generated submodule.

Every such element is a unit because I lies in the Jacobson radical, hence U=0.

cards.canonical_statement: If M→N→L→0 is an exact sequence of modules over a commutative ring and M,L are finitely generated, then N is finitely generated.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the finitely generated image of M and lift finite generators of L.
sketch_steps: Finite generation of M gives a finite generating family of the image of f.
Surjectivity of g allows finite generators of L to be lifted to N.
Subtract combinations of these lifts from an arbitrary element of N.
Exactness places the difference in the image of f, so the combined finite family generates N.

cards.canonical_statement: The image of a finitely generated submodule U under an R-linear map f:M→N is finitely generated.
cards.proof_strategy: Map a finite spanning family through the linear map.
sketch_steps: Choose finitely many generators of U.
Apply f to each of these generators.
Linearity sends generator expressions in U to combinations of their images.
Every element of the image has such an expression.
